paragraphs.text: Osteogenesis imperfecta type XIII is an autosomal recessive bone fragility disorder characterized by recurrent fractures, which may begin prenatally or at birth, or in childhood and mainly affect the lower limbs. Reported bone mineral density has varied: it was increased in some patients, normal in one, and decreased in others. Some severely affected patients also had marked short stature, bone deformities, joint hyperextensibility and umbilical hernia. The disorder results from deficient procollagen type I C-propeptide cleavage by BMP1.

paragraphs.text: Munns et al. (2004) described 3 unrelated children with an apparently novel bone fragility disorder associated with an idiopathic mineralization defect. Recurrent lower limb fractures started with weight bearing. On x-rays the children had increased metaphyseal trabeculation and normal to increased cortical thickness, with no evidence of rickets. Peripheral quantitative CT (pQCT) showed elevated radial cortical thickness and volumetric bone mineral density. Iliac bone biopsy showed a paucity of the birefringent lamellar bone pattern. Quantitative histomorphometry showed osteomalacia, with a prolonged mineralization lag time and a decreased mineral apposition rate. There was no biochemical evidence of abnormal calcium or phosphate metabolism. Munns et al. (2004) concluded that the disorder was a bone fragility disorder of moderate severity that tended to cause lower extremity fractures and was associated with osteoid accumulation due to an intrinsic mineralization defect. The patients lacked the phenotypic, radiologic and histomorphometric features of osteogenesis imperfecta, idiopathic juvenile osteoporosis and mild autosomal dominant osteopetrosis.

paragraphs.text: Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) reported 2 affected sibs born to first-cousin Egyptian parents. The proband (II-3), a 15-year-old girl, was referred with a history of recurrent fractures and bone deformities, beginning with a tibial fracture at birth. On examination she had a triangular face, broad forehead, wide palpebral fissures, long eyelashes, faint blue sclerae, long philtrum, thin lips and prominent ears. Her gross motor development was delayed, but her mental development was normal and she did not have dentinogenesis imperfecta or hearing loss. Other findings were a large umbilical hernia, generalized hypotonia, muscle wasting, nocturnal enuresis and generalized hirsutism, without skin hyperextensibility or bruising. She had a bowed humerus, radius and ulna, arachnodactyly, hyperextensible elbows, wrists and interphalangeal joints, limited knee movement, kyphoscoliosis and pectus carinatum. On x-rays she had platyspondyly, generalized decreased bone density and wormian bones. She had severe short stature (-11.5 SD), low weight and microcephaly (-3.0 SD), and her alkaline phosphatase was slightly elevated. Her 5-year-old brother (II-6) had bilateral femoral bowing on fetal ultrasound, and both femora were fractured at birth. He had recurrent fractures, generalized bone deformities, joint hyperextensibility, arachnodactyly and a large umbilical hernia, with normal mentality and no dentinogenesis imperfecta or hearing loss. An x-ray survey showed wormian bones of the skull, deformed long bones with lack of modeling, fractures and callus formation, scoliosis, platyspondyly and a wide symphysis pubis. He had short stature (-7.2 SD) and slightly elevated alkaline phosphatase. At 5 years, DEXA showed borderline osteoporosis at the spine (Z-score -1.63) and osteoporosis at the left femur (Z-score -2.75).

paragraphs.text: Fahiminiya et al. (2015) studied 4 unrelated children with a bone fragility disorder characterized by lower extremity fractures and a mineralization defect in bone tissue. On pQCT, all the children had elevated volumetric cortical bone mineral density. The mineralization defect involved bone tissue but not the growth plate.

One was a c.808A-G transition resulting in a met270-to-val (M270V) substitution. The other was c.1297G-T, which caused skipping of exon 10. In a zebrafish assay, the M270V variant was hypofunctional.
